song.artist: Stevie Ray Vaughan And Double Trouble
song.title: Couldnt Stand The Weather

guitar.evidence: Stevie Ray Vaughan's battered 1963/1959-hybrid Fender Stratocaster nicknamed 'Number One' is one of the most famous and well-documented guitars in blues-rock history.

tone.target: SRV Strat blues lead with sharp attack and light tube breakup
tone.profile: SRV Strat blues lead with sharp attack and light tube breakup
tone.summary: A clean Fender/AC30-style foundation using a light boost (TS style) for attack, followed by an AC30 model, compressed signal, wah accents, and spring reverb.
corrections: Use light breakup, not heavy overdrive

rig.name: Stevie Ray Vaughan And Double Trouble - Couldnt Stand The Weather - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Simulate the low-gain, high-mid punch of a Tube Screamer for attack and clarity.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated TS model; 'Boost' is used to simulate the mid-hump and gentle drive required.

alternatives.reason: If more grit than just boost is desired.

blocks.purpose: Provide the signature blues wah accents.
Kept inactive to avoid heavy distortion; used only if more grit is needed.
blocks.gap: The primary tone requires light breakup, not dedicated drive. This slot is kept for potential future use or slight saturation.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, articulate sound of a classic British clean amp (like an AC30), providing natural breakup.
blocks.gap: The ideal tone is Fender-based; however, the AC30 provides excellent clarity and mid-focus suitable for blues leads.

alternatives.reason: If a more distinctly American clean sound is preferred.

blocks.purpose: Provide a full-bodied, articulate cabinet sound.
blocks.gap: The ideal cab would be US/Fender style; this is the best available option for clarity and punch.

alternatives.reason: If a smaller, more focused American sound is desired.

blocks.purpose: Slightly boost the high-mids and treble to enhance the 'snap' and articulation required for blues leads.
Kept inactive as per the 'avoid' list (no chorus).
Provide the required short, classic spring reverb tail.
Kept inactive to avoid lush delay effects.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the UK cab for a US/Fender style IR to better match the desired American blues tone.

proposals.reason: The target sound is distinctly American blues, requiring a US cab character.
